questions.stem: When is the image formed by a concave mirror virtual, erect and larger than the object?
choices: Between the principal focus and the centre of curvature
Between the pole of the mirror and its principal focus
questions.solution: The image formed by a concave mirror is virtual, erect and larger than the object when the object is placed between the pole and the principal focus. This is because the rays diverge after reflection and appear to come from a point behind the mirror. The other options do not result in a virtual image.

questions.stem: What is the nature of the image formed by a plane mirror?
questions.solution: The image formed by a plane mirror is always virtual and erect. This is a well-known property of plane mirrors. The other options are incorrect because plane mirrors do not form real images, and the image is not inverted.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the diameter of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Aperture'. Aperture refers to the diameter of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror. Focal length is the distance from the pole to the principal focus, principal focus is where parallel rays converge after reflection, and centre of curvature is the center of the sphere that forms the mirror.

questions.stem: A light ray is incident on a convex mirror. Which of the following best describes the image formed?
questions.solution: The image formed by a convex mirror is always virtual, erect, and smaller than the object. This is a property of convex mirrors, which diverge light rays and cannot form real images. The other options are incorrect because convex mirrors do not form real images, and the image is not larger than the object.

questions.stem: A convex lens forms a real, inverted and enlarged image of an object. Where is the object most likely placed?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Between F and 2F'. When an object is placed between the focal point and twice the focal length of a convex lens, the lens forms a real, inverted, and enlarged image. If the object is at infinity, the image is tiny and formed at the focal point. If the object is at twice the focal length, the image is the same size as the object. If the object is between the focal point and the lens, the image is virtual and upright.

hi.stem: एक उत्तल लेंस एक वस्तु की वास्तविक, उल्टी और बड़ी छवि बनाता है। वस्तु संभवतः कहाँ रखी गई है?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर 'F और 2F के बीच' है। जब कोई वस्तु उत्तल लेंस के फोकस बिंदु और दो गुना फोकस दूरी के बीच रखी जाती है, तो लेंस एक वास्तविक, उल्टी और बड़ी छवि बनाता है। यदि वस्तु अनंत पर होती है, तो छवि छोटी होती है और फोकस बिंदु पर बनती है। यदि वस्तु दो गुना फोकस दूरी पर होती है, तो छवि वस्तु के बराबर आकार की होती है। यदि वस्तु फोकस बिंदु और लेंस के बीच होती है, तो छवि आभासी और सीधी होती है।

mr.stem: एक उत्तल लेंस वस्तूचे खरे, उलटे आणि वाढलेले छायाचित्र बनवते. वस्तू सर्वात जास्त जागी कुठे ठेवली जाते?
mr.solution: योग्य उत्तर 'F आणि 2F दरम्यान' आहे. जेव्हा वस्तू उत्तल लेंसच्या फोकस बिंदू आणि दुप्पट फोकस लांबी दरम्यान ठेवली जाते, तेव्हा लेंस खरे, उलटे आणि वाढलेले छायाचित्र बनवते. जर वस्तू अनंतावर असेल तर छायाचित्र लहान असते आणि फोकस बिंदूवर बनते. जर वस्तू दुप्पट फोकस लांबीवर असेल तर छायाचित्र वस्तूसारखेच असते. जर वस्तू फोकस बिंदू आणि लेंस दरम्यान असेल तर छायाचित्र आभासी आणि उलट असते.

questions.stem: A light ray travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium. What happens to the light ray?
choices: It bends away from the normal
It continues in a straight line
questions.solution: When a light ray travels from a rarer medium to a denser medium, it bends towards the normal. This is a fundamental law of refraction. The option 'It bends away from the normal' is incorrect because this happens when light travels from a denser to a rarer medium. The options 'It reflects back' and 'It continues in a straight line' are incorrect as they do not describe the behavior of refraction.

hi.stem: एक प्रकाश किरण एक दुर्लभ माध्यम से एक घनी माध्यम में यात्रा करती है। प्रकाश किरण पर क्या प्रभाव पड़ता है?
choices: यह सामान्य से दूर झुक जाती है
यह सामान्य की ओर झुक जाती है

questions.stem: A light ray travels from air into a glass slab. At the first surface, the ray bends towards the normal, and at the second surface, it bends away from the normal. Why does the emergent ray emerge parallel to the incident ray?
choices: The angles of incidence and refraction are equal at both surfaces
The refraction at both surfaces is equal and opposite
The light ray is not affected by the glass slab
The glass slab is too thin to affect the direction of the light ray
questions.solution: The emergent ray is parallel to the incident ray because the refraction at both surfaces is equal and opposite. At the first surface, the light bends towards the normal, and at the second surface, it bends away from the normal, resulting in the emergent ray being parallel. The other options are incorrect because the angles are not equal, the glass slab does affect the direction, and the thickness is not the reason for the parallelism.

hi.stem: एक प्रकाश किरण हवा से कांच के पट्टी में जाती है। पहली सतह पर, किरण सामान्य के निकट झुक जाती है, और दूसरी सतह पर, यह सामान्य से दूर झुक जाती है। अपवर्तित किरण आपतित किरण के समांतर क्यों निकलती है?

questions.stem: A convex lens forms a virtual, erect and diminished image. Where is the object located?
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'Between F and O'. A convex lens forms a virtual, erect, and diminished image when the object is placed between the focal point and the optical center. At 2F, the image is the same size as the object; between F and 2F, the image is enlarged; and at infinity, the image is formed at the focal point and is highly diminished.

hi.stem: एक उत्तल लेंस एक आभासी, सीधा और छोटा चित्र बनाता है। वस्तु कहाँ स्थित होती है?
hi.solution: सही उत्तर 'F और O के बीच' है। जब वस्तु फोकस बिंदु और ऑप्टिकल केंद्र के बीच रखी जाती है, तो एक उत्तल लेंस एक आभासी, सीधा और छोटा चित्र बनाता है। 2F पर चित्र वस्तु के बराबर आकार का होता है; F और 2F के बीच चित्र बड़ा होता है; और अनंत पर, चित्र फोकस बिंदु पर बनता है और बहुत छोटा होता है।

questions.stem: A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image. What is the reason for this?
choices: It has a positive focal length
It has a negative focal length
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'It diverges light rays'. A concave lens causes light rays to spread out, which results in a virtual, erect, and diminished image. The other options are incorrect because concave lenses do not converge light, they have a negative focal length, and positive focal lengths are associated with convex lenses.

questions.stem: A ray of light enters a convex lens from air. What happens to the ray if it passes through the optical centre of the lens?
choices: It bends away from the normal
It continues in a straight line without bending
questions.solution: A ray of light passing through the optical centre of a convex lens continues in a straight line without bending because the optical centre is a point where the lens does not cause any refraction. It does not bend towards or away from the normal because there is no change in direction at this point. Reflection is not involved in this scenario as the ray passes through the lens, not off its surface.

hi.stem: एक प्रकाश की किरण हवा से उत्तल लेंस में प्रवेश करती है। यदि किरण लेंस के ऑप्टिकल केंद्र से गुजरती है तो क्या होता है?

questions.stem: A ray of light is incident on a concave mirror at the principal focus. What happens to the reflected ray?
choices: It passes through the centre of curvature
It reflects back along the same path
It passes through the principal focus
It appears to diverge from the principal focus
questions.solution: The correct answer is 'It reflects back along the same path'. When a light ray is incident at the principal focus of a concave mirror, it reflects back along the same path due to the mirror's curvature and the properties of light reflection. The other options are incorrect because the ray does not pass through the center of curvature, does not pass through the principal focus again, and does not appear to diverge from the principal focus, which is a behavior associated with convex mirrors.

hi.critique: The translation is accurate, maintains the original meaning, and uses appropriate Hindi technical terms for optics.
